summary:
GetFire, developed by Team Parallax™, is an orbital active-fire harmonization and AI telemetry platform that unifies real-time wildfire observations from NASA EOSDIS FIRMS—specifically MODIS Collection 6.1 (1 km Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS Collection 2 (375 m Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20).

Wildfire responders face fragmented satellite streams with differing spatial resolutions, overpass times, and false-alarm profiles. GetFire addresses this challenge by indexing heterogeneous satellite detections into a unified Uber H3 Resolution-8 Discrete Global Grid, cross-validating co-located anomalies, and quantifying Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW) alongside Wooster et al. biomass combustion rates (kg/s). The platform pairs a self-pruning 100 MB SQLite WAL engine with a mobile-responsive aerospace interface featuring multi-layer orbital maps, thermal heat plumes, six scientific telemetry graphs, and a stateless Orbital AI Copilot that generates instant Incident Commander briefings.

By transforming raw multi-satellite infrared radiometry into actionable, cross-verified wildfire complexes, GetFire accelerates early ignition detection, resource triage, and climate-scale fire monitoring.
details:
What Does GetFire Do & How Does It Work?

GetFire is an enterprise-grade orbital Earth observation and active-fire intelligence platform developed by Team Parallax™. It ingests, harmonizes, and analyzes real-time thermal anomalies from NASA polar-orbiting satellites via NASA EOSDIS FIRMS:

  1. Multi-Sensor Satellite Ingestion: GetFire streams live active-fire telemetry from MODIS Collection 6.1 (1 km spatial resolution aboard Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS Collection 2 (375 m spatial resolution aboard Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20/JPSS-1). It supports both authenticated FIRMS Area API queries and keyless NASA EOSDIS 24-hour global CSV streams, enabling frictionless 1-click user synchronization (SYNC NASA LIVE).
  2. Uber H3 Spatial Harmonization & Deduplication: Because MODIS and VIIRS have different pixel footprints, swath widths, and overpass times, raw latitude/longitude points cannot be naively merged. GetFire projects every incoming detection onto an Uber H3 Resolution-8 Discrete Global Grid System (DGGS) (~0.74 km² hexagonal cells) and computes a deterministic SHA-1 observation hash (source + sensor + satellite + timestamp + coordinates) to prevent duplicate ingestion while identifying dual-sensor confirmed wildfire complexes.
  3. Radiometric & Biomass Modeling: For every anomaly and spatial cluster, GetFire analyzes Brightness Temperature (Kelvin) across middle-infrared channels (I4 / Band 21), Fire Radiative Power (FRP in Megawatts), diurnal Day/Night overpass splits, and estimated biomass combustion rates (kg/s) using the Wooster et al. (2005) radiometric coefficient (0.368 kg/MJ).
  4. Stateless Orbital AI Copilot & Incident Briefings: An integrated AI engine (supporting Google Gemini with a deterministic Local NASA Radiometric Heuristic fallback) synthesizes live viewport telemetry into structured Incident Commander Briefings, automated Euclidean/H3 fire complex classifications, and interactive Q&A—operating 100% statelessly without storing chat logs in the database.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Eliminating False Alarms & Sensor Blind Spots: VIIRS (375 m) catches small, nascent ignitions and night-time fire perimeters that 1 km sensors miss, while MODIS (1 km) provides high-saturation radiometric stability and a multi-decade climate baseline. Harmonizing both in H3 cells gives incident commanders high-confidence verification.
  • Zero-Maintenance Edge Reliability: Field deployments and community servers often crash when continuous satellite ingestion fills up disk storage. GetFire’s 100 MB Auto-Pruning SQLite Engine ensures the system can run 24/7 indefinitely on low-resource hardware without manual database cleanup.
  • Actionable Triage for First Responders & Researchers: Instead of overwhelming users with thousands of raw CSV rows, GetFire groups anomalies into ranked Spatial Wildfire Complexes, renders Thermal Plume Heatmaps, and provides 1-click verification links to NASA FIRMS and satellite imagery.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • NASA Data & Orbital Feeds: NASA EOSDIS FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 Terra/Aqua & VIIRS C2 Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20), OpenStreetMap Nominatim Geocoding, and Esri ArcGIS Global Imagery/Dark Gray Canvas/Topographic Tile Services.
  • Frontend Stack: React 19, Vite 8, JavaScript (ES2024), Leaflet & React-Leaflet (Canvas renderer + leaflet.heat radiative plume layer), custom SVG Scientific Telemetry Charts (24-Hour UTC Orbital Acquisition Curve, Kelvin- vs.-FRP Scatter Matrix, FRP Intensity Histogram, Diurnal/Sensor Split Meters, and Latitudinal Belt Profiles), and CSS3 (100dvh mobile-responsive aerospace glassmorphism UI).
  • Backend & Database Stack: Node.js (v22), Express.js, SQLite3 (better-sqlite3) running in Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) mode, and Uber h3-js for hexagonal spatial indexing.
  • AI & Intelligence Layer: Google Gemini 1.5 Flash REST API paired with a custom Local NASA Radiometric Heuristic & Spatial Clustering Engine.

How Is GetFire Creative & What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Deterministic 100 MB Self-Healing SQLite WAL Architecture: A key engineering factor our team considered was sustainable database storage under high-velocity global satellite streams (8,357+ active detections per sync). We engineered a real-time byte monitor that tracks getfire.db + getfire.db-wal + getfire.db-shm. Whenever storage crosses 100 MB, the engine automatically purges the oldest acquisition dates (FIFO) down to an 80 MB target and executes PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and VACUUM to physically reclaim disk pages.
  • Zero-Storage Stateless AI Architecture: Rather than bloating the database with chat history tables, our AI Copilot injects live, filtered orbital context directly from the active map viewport into each inference request, reserving 100% of disk capacity for scientific satellite telemetry.
  • Frictionless Public Accessibility: We removed administrative token barriers for data synchronization and replaced paid/watermarked map tiles with keyless Esri ArcGIS Dark Gray Canvas, Satellite, and Topographic basemaps so any judge, researcher, or responder can launch Mission Control on desktop or mobile and immediately analyze live NASA satellite fire data.
